subproblem.title: Orthonormal partner of a unit vector in a 2-plane
subproblem.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ, every linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) with dim Q = 2 and every u ∈ Q with ‖u‖ = 1, there is e ∈ Q with ‖e‖ = 1 and ⟨u, e⟩ = 0 such that every v ∈ Q satisfies v = ⟨v, u⟩u + ⟨v, e⟩e.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (u : Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 → u ∈ Q → ‖u‖ = 1 → ∃ e : Euclid P, e ∈ Q ∧ ‖e‖ = 1 ∧ inner ℝ u e = 0 ∧ ∀ v ∈ Q, v = inner ℝ v u • u + inner ℝ v e • e
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 2 (choice of e), stated for an arbitrary 2-dimensional subspace Q. Conventions: ⟨·,·⟩ is the real inner product of Euclid P, span is the ℝ-linear span, finrank is the real dimension.
1. Since ‖u‖ = 1, u ≠ 0 (‖0‖ = 0 ≠ 1) and ⟨u, u⟩ = ‖u‖² = 1 (real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq).
2. Because u ∈ Q, span{u} ≤ Q (Submodule.span_singleton_le_iff_mem). Because u ≠ 0, finrank span{u} = 1 (finrank_span_singleton). If span{u} = Q, then 1 = finrank span{u} = finrank Q = 2, which is false; hence span{u} < Q, and there is w ∈ Q with w ∉ span{u} (IsConcreteLE.exists_of_lt, the current name of SetLike.exists_of_lt).
3. Put e′ := w − ⟨w, u⟩u. Then e′ ∈ Q because w, u ∈ Q and Q is a subspace. Moreover e′ ≠ 0: if e′ = 0 then w = ⟨w, u⟩u ∈ span{u} (Submodule.smul_mem, Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self), contradicting the choice of w. Finally ⟨u, e′⟩ = ⟨u, w⟩ − ⟨w, u⟩⟨u, u⟩ = ⟨u, w⟩ − ⟨w, u⟩ = 0 by step 1 and symmetry of the real inner product (real_inner_comm).
4. As ‖e′‖ ≠ 0, put e := ‖e′‖⁻¹e′. Then e ∈ Q (Q is closed under scalar multiplication), ‖e‖ = ‖e′‖⁻¹‖e′‖ = 1, ⟨u, e⟩ = ‖e′‖⁻¹⟨u, e′⟩ = 0, and ⟨e, e⟩ = ‖e‖² = 1.
5. The two-element family (u, e) (Lean: ![u, e]) is orthonormal: ⟨u, u⟩ = ⟨e, e⟩ = 1 and ⟨u, e⟩ = ⟨e, u⟩ = 0 (orthonormal_iff_ite, checked on the four index pairs of Fin 2). Hence it is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so finrank span(range ![u, e]) = 2 (finrank_span_eq_card); since range ![u, e] = {u, e} (Matrix.range_cons, Matrix.range_empty, Set.union_empty), finrank span{u, e} = 2.
6. span{u, e} ≤ Q because u, e ∈ Q (Submodule.span_le). Q is finite-dimensional (a subspace of the finite-dimensional space Euclid P) and finrank span{u, e} = 2 = finrank Q, so span{u, e} = Q (Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq).
7. Let v ∈ Q. By step 6, v ∈ span{u, e}, so v = a·u + b·e for some a, b ∈ ℝ (Submodule.mem_span_pair). Taking inner products and using step 4: ⟨v, u⟩ = a⟨u, u⟩ + b⟨e, u⟩ = a and ⟨v, e⟩ = a⟨u, e⟩ + b⟨e, e⟩ = b. Hence v = ⟨v, u⟩u + ⟨v, e⟩e.
8. Thus e satisfies e ∈ Q, ‖e‖ = 1 (step 4), ⟨u, e⟩ = 0 (step 4) and the expansion of step 7, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: u ≠ 0 and ⟨u,u⟩ = 1; span{u} has dimension 1 < 2 = dim Q, so some w ∈ Q lies outside span{u}.
e′ := w − ⟨w,u⟩u is a nonzero vector of Q orthogonal to u; e := ‖e′‖⁻¹e′ is a unit vector of Q with ⟨u,e⟩ = 0.
(u, e) is orthonormal, hence independent, so span{u,e} ≤ Q has dimension 2 and equals Q.
Writing v ∈ Q as a·u + b·e and pairing with u and e gives a = ⟨v,u⟩, b = ⟨v,e⟩.

audit.reason: Prose and Lean type match, including membership in Q and the coordinate expansion. The proof establishes a vector outside span{u}, constructs and normalizes its nonzero orthogonal component, proves that the resulting pair spans Q by dimension, and derives both coefficients. All hypotheses are used correctly, with no circular dependence.

subproblem.title: Smoothness and derivative at r₀u of the polar map x ↦ (‖x‖, arctan(⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,u⟩))
subproblem.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ, all u, e ∈ ℝ^P and r₀ ∈ ℝ with ‖u‖ = 1, ⟨u, e⟩ = 0 and r₀ > 0, the map F : ℝ^P → ℝ² (Euclid 2), F(x) := (‖x‖, arctan(⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,u⟩)), is C¹ on the open half-space H := {x : ⟨x, u⟩ > 0}, and its Fréchet derivative at r₀u is DF(r₀u)h = (⟨u, h⟩, ⟨e, h⟩/r₀) for every h ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (u e : Euclid P) (r₀ : ℝ), ‖u‖ = 1 → inner ℝ u e = 0 → 0 < r₀ → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (fun x : Euclid P => (!₂[‖x‖, Real.arctan (inner ℝ x e / inner ℝ x u)] : Euclid 2)) {x : Euclid P | 0 < inner ℝ x u} ∧ ∀ h : Euclid P, fderiv ℝ (fun x : Euclid P => (!₂[‖x‖, Real.arctan (inner ℝ x e / inner ℝ x u)] : Euclid 2)) (r₀ • u) h = !₂[inner ℝ u h, inner ℝ e h / r₀]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 3 (coordinates: smoothness of F and the derivative DF(p), p = r₀u). Conventions: ⟨·,·⟩ is the real inner product; for a, b ∈ ℝ, (a, b) ∈ Euclid 2 is the point with coordinates a, b (Lean !₂[a, b]); F(x) := (‖x‖, arctan(⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,u⟩)), so the coordinates of F(x) are F(x)₀ = ‖x‖ and F(x)₁ = arctan(⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,u⟩); H := {x : 0 < ⟨x, u⟩}; p := r₀u.
1. H is open: it is the preimage of the open set (0, ∞) under the continuous map x ↦ ⟨x, u⟩ (isOpen_lt). Every x ∈ H is nonzero, since ⟨0, u⟩ = 0.
2. (Coordinate 0.) The norm of an inner product space is C^∞ at every nonzero point (contDiffAt_norm); by step 1 it is C¹ at every x ∈ H.
3. (Coordinate 1.) x ↦ ⟨x, e⟩ and x ↦ ⟨x, u⟩ are continuous linear, hence C^∞ (ContDiff.inner applied to contDiff_id and contDiff_const). For x ∈ H the denominator ⟨x, u⟩ is nonzero, so the quotient q(x) := ⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,u⟩ is C¹ at x (ContDiffAt.div). arctan is C^∞ on ℝ (Real.contDiff_arctan), so x ↦ arctan(q(x)) is C¹ at every x ∈ H (ContDiffAt.comp).
4. (F is C¹ on H.) A map into Euclid 2 = PiLp 2 (Fin 2 → ℝ) is C¹ on a set iff each of its two coordinate functions is (contDiffOn_piLp). By the simp identities (a, b)₀ = a and (a, b)₁ = b, the coordinates of F are the functions of steps 2 and 3, which are C¹ at each point of H, hence C¹ within H at each point of H. So F is C¹ on H. This is the first conclusion.
5. (Values at p.) ⟨p, u⟩ = r₀⟨u, u⟩ = r₀‖u‖² = r₀ > 0, so p ∈ H; ⟨p, e⟩ = r₀⟨u, e⟩ = 0; ‖p‖ = |r₀|·‖u‖ = r₀. Since H is open and F is C¹ on H, F is C¹ at p (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt) and hence differentiable at p (ContDiffAt.differentiableAt, 1 ≠ 0).
6. (Derivative of coordinate 0 at p.) x ↦ ‖x‖² has derivative h ↦ 2⟨p, h⟩ at p (hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq). Its value ‖p‖² = r₀² is nonzero, so x ↦ √(‖x‖²) has derivative h ↦ (1/(2√(‖p‖²)))·2⟨p, h⟩ at p (HasFDerivAt.sqrt). Since √(‖x‖²) = ‖x‖ for all x (Real.sqrt_sq, norm_nonneg) and √(r₀²) = r₀, this derivative is h ↦ (1/(2r₀))·2·r₀⟨u, h⟩ = ⟨u, h⟩. So x ↦ ‖x‖ has derivative h ↦ ⟨u, h⟩ (innerSL ℝ u) at p.
7. (Derivative of coordinate 1 at p.) a(x) := ⟨x, e⟩ has derivative h ↦ ⟨e, h⟩ and b(x) := ⟨x, u⟩ has derivative h ↦ ⟨u, h⟩ at p (continuous linear maps, using real_inner_comm). Since b(p) = r₀ ≠ 0, the map y ↦ y⁻¹ has derivative −(r₀²)⁻¹ at r₀ (hasDerivAt_inv), so by the chain rule x ↦ b(x)⁻¹ has derivative h ↦ −(r₀²)⁻¹⟨u, h⟩ at p (HasDerivAt.comp_hasFDerivAt). Since q(x) = a(x)·b(x)⁻¹, the product rule (HasFDerivAt.mul) gives Dq(p)h = a(p)·(−(r₀²)⁻¹⟨u, h⟩) + b(p)⁻¹⟨e, h⟩ = r₀⁻¹⟨e, h⟩, because a(p) = ⟨p, e⟩ = 0. Finally q(p) = 0/r₀ = 0, so by the chain rule for arctan (HasFDerivAt.arctan) x ↦ arctan(q(x)) has derivative h ↦ (1/(1 + 0²))·r₀⁻¹⟨e, h⟩ = r₀⁻¹⟨e, h⟩ at p.
8. (Identification of DF(p).) Let L := fderiv ℝ F p. For i ∈ {0, 1} the coordinate projection πᵢ : Euclid 2 → ℝ (EuclideanSpace.proj i) is continuous linear, so by the chain rule and step 5, πᵢ ∘ F has derivative πᵢ ∘ L at p. But πᵢ ∘ F is the i-th coordinate function of F, whose derivative at p was computed in step 6 (i = 0) and step 7 (i = 1); by uniqueness of the Fréchet derivative (HasFDerivAt.unique), π₀(L h) = ⟨u, h⟩ and π₁(L h) = r₀⁻¹⟨e, h⟩ = ⟨e, h⟩/r₀ for every h.
9. Two points of Euclid 2 with the same two coordinates are equal (extensionality over Fin 2), so L h = (⟨u, h⟩, ⟨e, h⟩/r₀) for every h ∈ ℝ^P. This is the second conclusion. ∎
proof_key_steps: H = {⟨x,u⟩ > 0} is open and excludes 0; the norm is C¹ away from 0 and arctan(⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,u⟩) is C¹ where ⟨x,u⟩ ≠ 0, so F is C¹ on H coordinatewise (contDiffOn_piLp).
At p = r₀u: ⟨p,u⟩ = r₀, ⟨p,e⟩ = 0, ‖p‖ = r₀, and F is differentiable at p.
D‖·‖(p)h = ⟨p,h⟩/‖p‖ = ⟨u,h⟩ via √(‖x‖²) and the derivative of ‖x‖².
Product rule for ⟨x,e⟩·⟨x,u⟩⁻¹ with ⟨p,e⟩ = 0 and arctan′(0) = 1 give D(arctan∘q)(p)h = ⟨e,h⟩/r₀.
Projecting fderiv F p onto both coordinates and using uniqueness of derivatives gives DF(p)h = (⟨u,h⟩, ⟨e,h⟩/r₀).

audit.reason: The type precisely states the half-space smoothness and pointwise derivative formula. The proof excludes zero and vanishing denominators, computes both derivatives with the required positivity assumptions, and identifies fderiv through coordinate projections and uniqueness. It correctly needs no unit-length hypothesis on e.

subproblem.title: Radial invariance forces G(t, α) = tγ(α) on the coordinate square
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, M, N ⊆ ℝ^P, p ∈ ℝ^P, ρ, r₀, s ∈ ℝ, F : ℝ^P → ℝ², G : ℝ² → ℝ^P and γ : ℝ → ℝ^P; put J := (r₀ − s, r₀ + s), I := (−s, s) and R := {w ∈ ℝ² : w₀ ∈ J, w₁ ∈ I}. Assume 0 < s < r₀; N is open and N ⊆ B_ρ(p); t·x ∈ M whenever x ∈ M ∩ B_ρ(p), t > 0 and t·x ∈ B_ρ(p); G is continuous on R; M ∩ N = G(R); F(G(w)) = w for every w ∈ R; and for every α ∈ I: ‖γ(α)‖ = 1, G(r₀, α) = r₀γ(α), and F(tγ(α)) = (t, α) for every t > 0. Then G(w) = w₀·γ(w₁) for every w ∈ R, and M ∩ N = {tγ(α) : t ∈ J, α ∈ I}, the image of J × I under (t, α) ↦ tγ(α).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (M N : Set (Euclid P)) (p : Euclid P) (ρ r₀ s : ℝ) (F : Euclid P → Euclid 2) (G : Euclid 2 → Euclid P) (γ : ℝ → Euclid P), 0 < s → s < r₀ → IsOpen N → N ⊆ ball p ρ → (∀ x ∈ M ∩ ball p ρ, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → t • x ∈ ball p ρ → t • x ∈ M) → ContinuousOn G {w : Euclid 2 | w 0 ∈ Ioo (r₀ - s) (r₀ + s) ∧ w 1 ∈ Ioo (-s) s} → M ∩ N = G '' {w : Euclid 2 | w 0 ∈ Ioo (r₀ - s) (r₀ + s) ∧ w 1 ∈ Ioo (-s) s} → (∀ w : Euclid 2, w 0 ∈ Ioo (r₀ - s) (r₀ + s) → w 1 ∈ Ioo (-s) s → F (G w) = w) → (∀ α ∈ Ioo (-s) s, ‖γ α‖ = 1 ∧ G !₂[r₀, α] = r₀ • γ α ∧ ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → F (t • γ α) = !₂[t, α]) → (∀ w : Euclid 2, w 0 ∈ Ioo (r₀ - s) (r₀ + s) → w 1 ∈ Ioo (-s) s → G w = w 0 • γ (w 1)) ∧ M ∩ N = (fun q : ℝ × ℝ => q.1 • γ q.2) '' (Ioo (r₀ - s) (r₀ + s) ×ˢ Ioo (-s) s)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 8 (radial structure), with the data produced in steps 5–7 of the parent proof turned into hypotheses. Conventions: J := (r₀ − s, r₀ + s), I := (−s, s); for w ∈ Euclid 2, w₀, w₁ are its coordinates (Lean w 0, w 1); ⟨⟨t, α⟩⟩ ∈ Euclid 2 is the point with coordinates (t, α) (Lean !₂[t, α]); R := {w : w₀ ∈ J, w₁ ∈ I}; B_r(y) is the open ball. Note ⟨⟨t, α⟩⟩ ∈ R iff t ∈ J and α ∈ I (simp), r₀ − s > 0 (as s < r₀), and r₀ ∈ J (as s > 0).
1. Fix α ∈ I and let A := {t ∈ ℝ : t ∈ J and G(⟨⟨t, α⟩⟩) = tγ(α)}. The map t ↦ ⟨⟨t, α⟩⟩ is continuous (each coordinate is continuous; PiLp.continuous_toLp) and maps J into R, so φ₁(t) := G(⟨⟨t, α⟩⟩) is continuous on J (ContinuousOn.comp); φ₂(t) := tγ(α) is continuous on ℝ.
2. (r₀ ∈ A.) r₀ ∈ J, and G(⟨⟨r₀, α⟩⟩) = r₀γ(α) by hypothesis.
3. (A is open.) Let t ∈ A and x := tγ(α) = G(⟨⟨t, α⟩⟩). Since ⟨⟨t, α⟩⟩ ∈ R, x ∈ G(R) = M ∩ N. As N is open, choose η₀ > 0 with B_{η₀}(x) ⊆ N (Metric.isOpen_iff), and put η := min(η₀, t − (r₀ − s)) > 0 (t ∈ J). Let t′ ∈ ℝ with |t′ − t| < η. Then t′ ≥ t − |t′ − t| > t − (t − (r₀ − s)) = r₀ − s > 0, and t > r₀ − s > 0.
 (a) y := t′γ(α) ∈ N: ‖y − x‖ = ‖(t′ − t)γ(α)‖ = |t′ − t|·‖γ(α)‖ = |t′ − t| < η ≤ η₀, so y ∈ B_{η₀}(x) ⊆ N; in particular y ∈ B_ρ(p).
 (b) y ∈ M: x ∈ M and x ∈ N ⊆ B_ρ(p), so x ∈ M ∩ B_ρ(p); c := t′/t > 0 and c·x = (t′/t)·tγ(α) = y ∈ B_ρ(p); the radial hypothesis gives y ∈ M.
 (c) Hence y ∈ M ∩ N = G(R), so y = G(w) for some w ∈ R. Then w = F(G(w)) = F(y) = F(t′γ(α)) = ⟨⟨t′, α⟩⟩ (t′ > 0). Therefore ⟨⟨t′, α⟩⟩ = w ∈ R, i.e. t′ ∈ J, and G(⟨⟨t′, α⟩⟩) = G(w) = y = t′γ(α). So t′ ∈ A.
 Thus the ball of radius η about t lies in A, and A is open.
4. (closure(A) ∩ J ⊆ A.) Let t ∈ closure(A) ∩ J. As J is open and contains t, φ₁ and φ₂ are continuous at t (ContinuousOn.continuousAt with isOpen_Ioo.mem_nhds). Since t ∈ closure(A), the filter 𝓝[A] t is nontrivial (mem_closure_iff_nhdsWithin_neBot). Along 𝓝[A] t we have φ₁ → φ₁(t) and φ₂ → φ₂(t) (nhdsWithin_le_nhds); since φ₁ = φ₂ on A, also φ₁ → φ₂(t) (Tendsto.congr' with eventually_nhdsWithin_of_forall). Limits in the Hausdorff space Euclid P are unique (tendsto_nhds_unique), so φ₁(t) = φ₂(t), i.e. t ∈ A.
5. (Connectedness.) J is preconnected (isPreconnected_Ioo), A is open (step 3), J ∩ A ∋ r₀ is nonempty (step 2) and closure(A) ∩ J ⊆ A (step 4). Hence J ⊆ A (IsPreconnected.subset_of_closure_inter_subset). Since α ∈ I was arbitrary: G(⟨⟨t, α⟩⟩) = tγ(α) for all t ∈ J and α ∈ I.
6. (First conclusion.) Let w ∈ R. Then w = ⟨⟨w₀, w₁⟩⟩ (both sides have the same coordinates; extensionality over Fin 2), w₀ ∈ J and w₁ ∈ I, so G(w) = G(⟨⟨w₀, w₁⟩⟩) = w₀γ(w₁) by step 5.
7. (Second conclusion.) M ∩ N = G(R). If x ∈ G(R), x = G(w) with w ∈ R, then x = w₀γ(w₁) by step 6 with (w₀, w₁) ∈ J × I. Conversely, if (t, α) ∈ J × I, then ⟨⟨t, α⟩⟩ ∈ R and tγ(α) = G(⟨⟨t, α⟩⟩) ∈ G(R) by step 5. Hence M ∩ N = {tγ(α) : (t, α) ∈ J × I}, the image of J ×ˢ I under q ↦ q.1·γ(q.2). ∎
proof_key_steps: Fix α ∈ I; A := {t ∈ J : G(t,α) = tγ(α)} contains r₀ by hypothesis.
A is open: near t ∈ A, y = t′γ(α) stays in the open set N, lies in M by radial invariance (y = (t′/t)·tγ(α)), so y = G(w) with w ∈ R, and F∘G = id with F(t′γ(α)) = (t′,α) forces w = (t′,α), t′ ∈ A.
closure(A) ∩ J ⊆ A because t ↦ G(t,α) and t ↦ tγ(α) are continuous on the open interval J and limits are unique.
J is preconnected, so J ⊆ A; hence G(w) = w₀γ(w₁) on R.
M ∩ N = G(R) is therefore the image of J × I under (t,α) ↦ tγ(α).

audit.reason: The statements agree exactly. The proof establishes nonemptiness, openness and relative closedness of A before invoking connectedness. Nearby points enter M through positive radial scaling; chart membership and F∘G identify their coordinates without assuming radial extension. Both conclusions follow. The parent establishes the strong F(tγ(α)) hypothesis independently by homogeneity.

subproblem.title: Range of the derivative of (t, α) ↦ tγ(α)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, γ : ℝ → ℝ^P, G : ℝ² → ℝ^P (ℝ² = Euclid 2), S ⊆ ℝ² open and t, α ∈ ℝ with (t, α) ∈ S. If G(w) = w₀·γ(w₁) for every w ∈ S, γ is differentiable at α and t ≠ 0, then the range of the Fréchet derivative DG(t, α) equals (as a set) the linear span of γ(α) and γ′(α), where γ′ = deriv γ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (γ : ℝ → Euclid P) (G : Euclid 2 → Euclid P) (S : Set (Euclid 2)) (t α : ℝ), IsOpen S → !₂[t, α] ∈ S → (∀ w ∈ S, G w = w 0 • γ (w 1)) → DifferentiableAt ℝ γ α → t ≠ 0 → Set.range (fderiv ℝ G !₂[t, α]) = (Submodule.span ℝ {γ α, deriv γ α} : Set (Euclid P))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 9 (tangent planes: DG(w) = DG̃(w) for G̃(w′) = w′₀γ(w′₁), product rule, and the range computation). Conventions: for w ∈ Euclid 2, w₀, w₁ are its coordinates (Lean w 0, w 1); ⟨⟨a, b⟩⟩ ∈ Euclid 2 is the point with coordinates (a, b) (Lean !₂[a, b]); ω := ⟨⟨t, α⟩⟩, so ω₀ = t and ω₁ = α; γ′ := deriv γ; DG := fderiv ℝ G.
1. Let G̃(w) := w₀·γ(w₁). Since S is open and ω ∈ S, S is a neighbourhood of ω on which G = G̃; hence G =ᶠ[𝓝 ω] G̃ (Filter.eventually_of_mem with IsOpen.mem_nhds), and therefore DG(ω) = DG̃(ω) (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).
2. The coordinate maps π₀(w) = w₀ and π₁(w) = w₁ are continuous linear maps Euclid 2 → ℝ (EuclideanSpace.proj 0 and proj 1), so each is its own derivative at ω (ContinuousLinearMap.hasFDerivAt).
3. γ is differentiable at α = π₁(ω), so γ has derivative k ↦ k·γ′(α) at α (DifferentiableAt.hasDerivAt, HasDerivAt.hasFDerivAt). By the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp), w ↦ γ(w₁) has derivative h ↦ h₁·γ′(α) at ω.
4. By the product rule for a scalar function times a vector function (HasFDerivAt.smul), G̃ = π₀·(γ∘π₁) has derivative h ↦ π₀(ω)·(h₁·γ′(α)) + h₀·γ(π₁(ω)) at ω. Hence, using step 1 and HasFDerivAt.fderiv, for every h ∈ Euclid 2:
 DG(ω)h = h₀·γ(α) + (t·h₁)·γ′(α).
5. (range ⊆ span.) For every h, DG(ω)h = a·γ(α) + b·γ′(α) with a := h₀, b := t·h₁, so DG(ω)h ∈ span{γ(α), γ′(α)} (Submodule.mem_span_pair).
6. (span ⊆ range.) Let v ∈ span{γ(α), γ′(α)}; by Submodule.mem_span_pair, v = a·γ(α) + b·γ′(α) for some a, b ∈ ℝ. Since t ≠ 0, take h := ⟨⟨a, b/t⟩⟩. Then h₀ = a, h₁ = b/t and t·(b/t) = b, so by step 4 DG(ω)h = a·γ(α) + b·γ′(α) = v. Hence v ∈ range DG(ω).
7. By steps 5 and 6 (set extensionality), Set.range DG(⟨⟨t, α⟩⟩) equals the carrier of span{γ(α), γ′(α)}. ∎
proof_key_steps: G agrees with G̃(w) = w₀γ(w₁) on the open neighbourhood S of (t,α), so DG(t,α) = DG̃(t,α).
Chain rule and product rule: DG(t,α)h = h₀γ(α) + (t h₁)γ′(α).
Every value lies in span{γ(α), γ′(α)}; conversely aγ(α) + bγ′(α) is the value at h = (a, b/t) since t ≠ 0.

audit.reason: The type matches the stated equality of sets. Openness yields local equality with the model map, differentiability of γ justifies the chain and product rules, and t ≠ 0 supplies the explicit preimage (a,b/t). Both range inclusions are proved without requiring independence of γ(α) and γ′(α).

subproblem.title: Shrinking a local inverse chart to a coordinate square
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, M, U, N₀ ⊆ ℝ^P, O ⊆ ℝ² (Euclid 2), F : ℝ^P → ℝ², G : ℝ² → ℝ^P, p ∈ ℝ^P and r₀ > 0. Assume U is open, F is continuous on U, O and N₀ are open, F(p) = (r₀, 0), F(p) ∈ O, p ∈ N₀ ⊆ U, G(O) = M ∩ N₀ and F(G(w)) = w for all w ∈ O. For s ∈ ℝ let R_s := {w ∈ ℝ² : w₀ ∈ (r₀ − s, r₀ + s), w₁ ∈ (−s, s)}. Then there are s ∈ ℝ with 0 < s < r₀ and an open set N ⊆ ℝ^P with p ∈ N ⊆ U, R_s ⊆ O and M ∩ N = G(R_s).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (M U N₀ : Set (Euclid P)) (O : Set (Euclid 2)) (F : Euclid P → Euclid 2) (G : Euclid 2 → Euclid P) (p : Euclid P) (r₀ : ℝ), 0 < r₀ → IsOpen U → ContinuousOn F U → IsOpen O → IsOpen N₀ → F p = !₂[r₀, 0] → F p ∈ O → p ∈ N₀ → N₀ ⊆ U → G '' O = M ∩ N₀ → (∀ w ∈ O, F (G w) = w) → ∃ (s : ℝ) (N : Set (Euclid P)), 0 < s ∧ s < r₀ ∧ IsOpen N ∧ p ∈ N ∧ N ⊆ U ∧ {w : Euclid 2 | w 0 ∈ Ioo (r₀ - s) (r₀ + s) ∧ w 1 ∈ Ioo (-s) s} ⊆ O ∧ M ∩ N = G '' {w : Euclid 2 | w 0 ∈ Ioo (r₀ - s) (r₀ + s) ∧ w 1 ∈ Ioo (-s) s}
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 6 (square and the set N), stated for abstract local-inverse data (O, N₀, G) of a map F continuous on U. Conventions: for w ∈ Euclid 2, w₀ and w₁ are its coordinates (Lean w 0, w 1); (a, b) ∈ Euclid 2 is the point with coordinates a, b (Lean !₂[a, b]); B_ε(y) is the open ball; R_s := {w : w₀ ∈ (r₀ − s, r₀ + s) and w₁ ∈ (−s, s)}.
1. Since O is open and F(p) ∈ O, there is ε > 0 with B_ε(F(p)) ⊆ O (Metric.isOpen_iff).
2. Put s := min(ε, r₀)/4. Then s > 0 (ε > 0, r₀ > 0), s ≤ r₀/4 < r₀, and s ≤ ε/4.
3. (R_s ⊆ O.) Let w ∈ R_s. Then |w₀ − r₀| < s and |w₁| < s, so (w₀ − r₀)² < s² and w₁² < s². Because F(p) = (r₀, 0), the Euclidean distance is dist(w, F(p)) = √((w₀ − r₀)² + (w₁ − 0)²) (EuclideanSpace.dist_eq, Fin.sum_univ_two, Real.dist_eq, sq_abs). Now (w₀ − r₀)² + w₁² < 2s² ≤ 2(ε/4)² = ε²/8 < ε², so dist(w, F(p)) < ε (Real.sqrt_lt', ε > 0). Hence w ∈ B_ε(F(p)) ⊆ O.
4. (R_s is open.) R_s is the intersection of the preimages of the open intervals (r₀ − s, r₀ + s) and (−s, s) under the continuous coordinate maps w ↦ w₀ and w ↦ w₁ (isOpen_Ioo.preimage, IsOpen.inter).
5. (The set N.) Define N := N₀ ∩ (U ∩ F⁻¹(R_s)). Since F is continuous on the open set U and R_s is open, U ∩ F⁻¹(R_s) is open (ContinuousOn.isOpen_inter_preimage); as N₀ is open, N is open. Clearly N ⊆ U.
6. (p ∈ N.) p ∈ N₀ by hypothesis, p ∈ U because N₀ ⊆ U, and F(p) = (r₀, 0) ∈ R_s because r₀ − s < r₀ < r₀ + s and −s < 0 < s (s > 0). Hence p ∈ N.
7. (M ∩ N ⊆ G(R_s).) Let x ∈ M ∩ N. Then x ∈ M ∩ N₀ = G(O), so x = G(w) for some w ∈ O. Then F(x) = F(G(w)) = w, and x ∈ F⁻¹(R_s) gives w = F(x) ∈ R_s. Hence x = G(w) ∈ G(R_s).
8. (G(R_s) ⊆ M ∩ N.) Let w ∈ R_s. By step 3, w ∈ O, so G(w) ∈ G(O) = M ∩ N₀; thus G(w) ∈ M, G(w) ∈ N₀, G(w) ∈ U (N₀ ⊆ U) and F(G(w)) = w ∈ R_s. Hence G(w) ∈ N₀ ∩ (U ∩ F⁻¹(R_s)) = N, and G(w) ∈ M ∩ N.
9. By steps 2–8, s and N satisfy 0 < s < r₀, N open, p ∈ N, N ⊆ U, R_s ⊆ O and M ∩ N = G(R_s). ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose ε > 0 with B_ε(F p) ⊆ O and s := min(ε, r₀)/4, so 0 < s < r₀ and s ≤ ε/4.
Every w in the square R_s has dist(w, (r₀,0))² < 2s² < ε², so R_s ⊆ O; R_s is open.
N := N₀ ∩ (U ∩ F⁻¹(R_s)) is open (F continuous on open U), contains p, and lies in U.
Using G(O) = M ∩ N₀ and F∘G = id on O, x ∈ M ∩ N iff x = G(w) with w ∈ R_s.

audit.reason: Every local-inverse hypothesis appears in both statements. The explicit choice s = min(ε,r₀)/4 gives the required square containment. The constructed N is open, contains p and lies in U; both image inclusions follow from the stated inverse identities. No extra continuity of G or manifold hypothesis is assumed.
